items.title: A Moser diffeomorphism pulling omega back to omega_0, fixing the boundary
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Journal de l'École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.195
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:pullback_to_nu0` at source lines 1501-1504: if lambda is C2-close enough to lambda_0 then there is a diffeomorphism kappa fixing the boundary with kappa^* omega = omega_0, and kappa is C1-close to the identity as lambda approaches lambda_0. The author's proof (source lines 1506-1580) is a complete Moser-trick construction on a surface with boundary: it first checks that the interpolating forms are symplectic with the right orientation and uniformly close (line 1507), sets up the isotopy equation d(X interior omega_t + nu - nu_0) = 0 and chooses the defining equation for X_t with a function f still to be determined (lines 1509-1523), computes in collar coordinates the structure functions h_1, h_2, h_3 together with the differential identity they satisfy (lines 1525-1539), chooses f explicitly as minus the integral of h_1 near the boundary and zero further out, and then estimates the two components of X_t, obtaining S_t = 0 and a formula for R_t with a C0-small numerator that makes X_t C1-small, smoothly extendable and boundary-vanishing (lines 1540-1577); the flow then gives the conclusion (lines 1578-1579). The statement contains only the existence and the convergence, and the whole quantitative part is invisible in it.
